subject: Urgent: Reserved throughput shortfall & GPU pool saturation impacting NimbusPay
messages:
From: Maya Rao <maya@nimbo-pay.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: platform@nimbo-pay.com
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden latency and error surge on reserved pool (impacting payments)

Vivek —

Quick note from production: since ~14:00 PDT we've seen token latencies spike on our reserved endpoint and an increase in 500/429 errors. Throughput is below the committed curve in the SLA window; customers are seeing payment authorization delays. Our engineering team attached a short log with the most recent 500s and a CSV of per-minute throughput. This is causing manual intervention across merchant checkout pages.

Can you confirm whether this is a capacity scheduling/regression issue on Redwood's side or a misconfiguration in our routing? We provisioned dedicated capacity (reserved) for this workload — we need an initial root-cause or a mitigation path within the next 6 hours.

Attachments: nimbuspay_error_samples.log, throughput-metrics-08014.csv

Thanks,
Maya Rao
Head of Platform, NimbusPay

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya@nimbo-pay.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden latency and error surge on reserved pool (impacting payments)

Maya — thanks for the fast heads-up and for the logs. I'm escalating immediately and pulling ops and infra on call. Initial checklist: reserved capacity mapping, current pool utilization, any recent model rollouts or kernel changes, and autoscaler events.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Can you confirm the route and model id the traffic is hitting (token prefix shown in the sample is helpful)?
- Are you seeing a traffic spike or a change in request sizing/seq length distributions since 12:00 PDT?

I'll update within 30 minutes with a status. We're treating this as a P1.

— Vivek
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 16:44:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden latency and error surge on reserved pool (impacting payments)

Quick findings from the runtime team (initial probe):
- Pool utilization: one dedicated pool in us-west-2 is at sustained 96% GPU utilization for the past 45m.
- Autoscaler: no recent scale-up events triggered due to the pool being pinned by 'reserved' instances; burst capacity is available but requires policy approval for this account.
- Recent change: yesterday evening we rolled a kernel tweak that slightly changes KV cache eviction heuristics; we haven't seen production impact elsewhere yet but can't rule it out.
- Errors: the 500s map to OOM-like memory pressure in the inferencer (OOM adjacent), and many 429s coincide with per-pool queue depth thresholds being hit.

Proposed immediate mitigations (can be executed in parallel):
1) Authorize temporary burst of 4 GPUs from the burst pool to NimbusPay's reserved pool (expected to reduce queueing and 429s within 10m).
2) Roll back the kernel tweak to yesterday's kernel on the affected pool (risk: short restart window).
3) Configure a lightweight routing fallback to a compatible lower-RAM model variant for non-critical authorization paths.

I'll draft a short canary fallback plan if you want to push option (3) immediately.

— Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Rao <maya@nimbo-pay.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Aug 2028 09:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency and error surge on reserved pool (impacting payments)

Maya — quick update and proposed plan of action (planning for a 2-hour mitigation window starting now):
- Authorization: marketing/partnerships approved temporary burst; I'm escalating billing to approve the charge cap. Marcus, please confirm the cap we can apply.
- Execution: Karthik will trigger burst attach (option 1) and simultaneously apply a routing rule: 10% of traffic -> lower-memory variant (option 3) as a canary. We'll monitor 429/500 rates over 15m windows.
- Rollback: if burst attach does not improve error rates or introduces instability, we will schedule a kernel rollback with a 5-minute maintenance hint to NimbusPay (preferred after business hours if avoidable).

Attachments: canary-fallback-plan-v1.pdf

Action items:
- Marcus: approve burst cap now.
- Karthik: prepare attach script and runbook.
- Vivek: communicate timeline to NimbusPay and set expectation for 15m check-ins.

— Laura
Senior CS Lead, Redwood Inference

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Maya Rao <maya@nimbo-pay.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Aug 2028 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden latency and error surge on reserved pool (impacting payments) — decision and exec note

Maya — thank you for your patience. Quick readout and exec decision:

Status summary:
- We attached 4 GPUs from the burst pool at 09:12 PDT yesterday; queue depth reduced and 429s dropped by ~82% within 12 minutes.
- The short canary (10% traffic to lower-RAM variant) showed 0.6% higher token latency but no increase in error rate; full traffic still prefers primary path.
- The underlying cause is a combination of the new KV eviction tweak increasing memory pressure on longer seq-length requests and an unanticipated traffic pattern from NimbusPay during their peak reconciliation window.

Decision and next steps:
1) Short term: keep the burst attach for 72 hours while we monitor and run a load profile replay against the kernel tweak. NimbusPay will not be billed for the burst during this window — Redwood will absorb as a goodwill credit (Marcus, please record expense under account relief).
2) Medium term: revert the KV eviction tweak on the affected pool if load-replay reproduces the pressure; otherwise we'll ship a targeted patch to improve memory accounting.
3) Product follow-up: Ops + PM (Karthik and Hannah) to produce an autoscaling policy exception for reserved pools that allows a controlled, pre-approved burst for top-tier customers to avoid manual approvals in P1 windows.

Maya, I will schedule a 30-minute bridge with engineering and CS at 11:00 PDT tomorrow to walk through the postmortem and recommended permanent remediation. Appreciate the quick coordination here — apologies for the disruption.

— Vivek
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
